newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks move up on lack of sellers.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks move up on lack of sellers.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed higher on Monday as sellers held back after last week's sweeping elections win by the ruling coalition, brokers said.
The all share index closed 1.03 points up at 634.33. Price gains led declines by 25 to five, but a fall in two highly capitalised blue chips restrained the index, brokers said.
Dankotuawa Porcelain rose 2.25 rupees to 29.75, Horana Plantations one to 26. Blue chips Development Finance and Hatton National Bank fell 2.50 and six rupees to 250 and 244, respectively.
"It was impossible to trade as sellers held out for premiums," said Subram Ramasamy of Bartleet Mallory Stock Brokers. Turnover was 46.7 million rupees on 3.1 million shares.

Sellers have moved to the sidelines after the government's convincing victory at last Friday's local polls, brokers said. Gordon Nadesan, a trader at brokerage CT Smith, said buyers were unwilling to pay premiums and also were cautious due to the end of the March 31 accounting year being one week away.
"Buyers know that the settlement date on current purchases will be after books close for the year," he said.
